input: Pitch a new product feature to my team

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing what the feature is and what problem it solves defines the entire content of the pitch — without this, nothing can be planned.
The audience's roles (engineers, designers, executives, mixed) dictates the level of technical depth, the language used, and what they need to be persuaded of.
Whether this is a scheduled meeting, a casual stand-up, or an async presentation changes the format and level of formality required.
A hard time limit (e.g. 5 mins vs. 30 mins) drastically changes how much detail can be included and how the pitch must be structured.
The deliverable format — slide deck, live verbal pitch, written doc, demo — determines what actually needs to be produced.
Knowing the desired outcome (get a green light, gather feedback, assign owners, spark discussion) shapes what the pitch needs to accomplish and how it should close.
The tone and framing (data-driven, user-story-led, business-case-focused) should match the user's style and what will resonate most with this specific team.

gold.taskTitle: Pitch a new product feature to my team
gold.taskDescription: Prepare and deliver a compelling pitch for a new product feature to the user's team.

questions.title: What feature are you pitching, and what problem does it solve?
questions.description: Identify the specific feature and the core user or business problem it addresses.

questions.title: Who exactly will be in the room for this pitch?
questions.description: Clarify the roles and seniority of the audience to tailor depth and language appropriately.

questions.title: Is this a formal meeting, a stand-up, or something else?
questions.description: Understand the setting and occasion to set the right level of formality and structure.

questions.title: How much time do you have to deliver the pitch?
questions.description: Determine the time constraint to plan how much content can realistically be covered.

questions.title: What format do you need — slides, a doc, a live demo, verbal?
questions.description: Establish the physical or digital deliverable that needs to be created.

questions.title: What outcome do you need from the team by the end?
questions.description: Define what a successful pitch looks like — approval, feedback, task assignment, or buy-in.

questions.title: Should the pitch lead with data, user stories, or business impact?
questions.description: Identify the preferred framing and tone that will resonate most with this team.
